title: A glowing gas spectrum
hook: Explore the evidence behind a cosmic question.

knows: Light and gravity help astronomers study the universe.
doesNotKnow: Excited atoms can emit photons at characteristic wavelengths. A thin glowing gas can therefore produce bright emission lines rather than an entirely continuous spectrum.

misconception: A learner may choose: Only a featureless black image
objective: Use the visual model to reason about: A hot, thin gas emits light at particular wavelengths. What can appear in its spectrum?

claims.text: Question, correct answer and explanation: A hot, thin gas emits light at particular wavelengths. What can appear in its spectrum? Bright emission lines. Excited atoms can emit photons at characteristic wavelengths. A thin glowing gas can therefore produce bright emission lines rather than an entirely continuous spectrum.
Visual caption: Hot gas: bright lines. The SVG is a conceptual illustration, not measured data or a scale model.
